explanations: Inside the loop over employees, entries.filter(...) scans every timesheet entry for each employee, making the run O(employees x entries). For a company with 20k employees and ~200k entries that is billions of comparisons per run. groupByEmployee already exists to bucket entries in one pass, but runPayroll never uses it. Tax bands, by contrast, are sorted once up front, so they are not the hot spot.

weeklyHours sums hours per isoWeek and overtime is computed per week. Week A: 40 x $20 + 5 x $30 = $950. Week B: 30 x $20 = $600. Total $1,550. Overtime is not averaged over the period, the multiplier is 1.5 not 2, and only hours above 40 get the premium.

withholdingCents is marginal: band one taxes 1,000,000 x 0.10 = 100,000; band two taxes (1,500,000 - 1,000,000) x 0.20 = 100,000. Total 200,000. It never applies a single rate to the whole gross, and band two only covers the portion above 1,000,000.

runPayroll throws an Error naming the region and employee when sortedBands.get returns undefined. Because slips are only returned at the end, the whole run fails rather than returning partial results. There is no zero-tax default, skip, or fallback region.
